S64.01.note: VS Code only reads a pasted link, not the live browser page; the live-page reading in the Chrome side panel (apps/extension) was not traced to a label. The plus button's own label was not confirmed.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code and click the plus button in the composer to open the plus menu.
Click "Web page" and paste a full https:// link into the box that opens.
Click OK in the box. The page is read once from that link and its text is attached to the next message.
Type a question about the page and send it. Compare: the answer uses the text of the pasted link, not the page open in your browser tab.
S64.01.where: Chat composer > plus menu > Web page (the link box says "Attach a web page")

S64.02.needs: a Chrome browser with the AGI extension, and VS Code open with the AGI extension
S64.02.note: The exact button label in the Chrome dialog that starts the send was not found in the code; the destination name "VS Code" was found.
steps: In Chrome with the AGI extension, highlight some text on a web page.
Send the selection from the AGI extension to the "VS Code" destination; the dialog says it opens the AGI composer in VS Code via a vscode:// link.
In VS Code, the AGI chat composer opens with a draft that starts "Selected in the browser, from" followed by the page address and the highlighted text.
Type a question after it and send. Compare: the answer uses the highlighted text as context.
S64.02.where: Chrome extension side panel > select text on a web page > send it to "VS Code" (the VS Code chat composer then gets the text)

S64.06.note: Same path as S64.01: the page is the pasted link, read once, not the open browser tab. The plus button's own label was not confirmed.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code and click the plus button in the composer.
Click "Web page" and paste a link to a page with known text.
Type a free-form question about that text (for example a fact that appears only on the page) and send.
Compare: the answer uses the content of the pasted page.
S64.06.where: Chat composer > plus menu > Web page, then type a free-form question

S64.10.note: No control in the VS Code chat lets the assistant open a web address. Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for openExternal (only used for app links such as upgrade, help and artifact pages) and found browser_navigate only in apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs, which is not part of the VS Code panel.

S64.14.note: No website search control was found in the VS Code app. The nearest control is the plus menu item "Browse the web" (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), which is a general web search through the CLI and not a search on a site. Website search tools (browser_find in apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs) are not in the VS Code panel.

S64.15.note: No form-filling control found in apps/extension-vscode/src. browser_fill_form exists only in the CLI tool list (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs) and the Chrome extension, not the VS Code panel.

S64.16.note: No multi-step website task control found in apps/extension-vscode/src. The browser tool list (browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type and others) is in apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs, not the VS Code panel. Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for browser and web terms.

S64.18.needs: a working local runtime, and a request that uses a browser tool, which depends on the runtime and route
S64.18.note: The VS Code panel shows tool rows generically (toolCallStart and toolCallEnd in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts). No browser-specific timeline was found. Whether browser tools run from the VS Code panel was not verified.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code and send a request that needs a tool.
Watch the reply while it runs: each tool call appears as its own row in the chat as it starts and ends.
Compare: each row shows the tool's name and a summary; a web action appears with a globe icon (the icon map lists browser and web fetch tools as globe).
S64.18.where: Chat panel > send a message that makes the assistant use a tool > tool rows in the reply

S64.25.note: No pause control was found; only stop. The stop is for the whole reply, not a browser task specifically. The Escape setting is agiWorkforce.composer.escapeStops (default off) in apps/extension-vscode/package.json.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code and send a request that takes a while.
While the reply is still being written, click the square "Stop response" button beside the composer.
Compare: the reply stops and the button changes to "Stopping" until the stop finishes.
Optional: turn on the setting "Stop the active response when Escape is pressed in the composer" and press Escape in the composer while a reply runs.
S64.25.where: Chat panel > send a message > Stop response button shown at the composer while the reply is running

S64.32.note: No browser-task summary screen found in apps/extension-vscode/src. The turn ends with the normal reply in the chat. The closest summary code is the session receipt (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/sessionReceipt.ts), which lists file changes and approvals, not browser actions.
